SubTopics: Analyze and interpret chemical reactions to determine if the total number of atoms in the reactants and products support the Law of Conservation of Mass.
Content: A scientist conducted an experiment with a magnesium sulfate (`text(MgSO)_4`) solution and a sodium carbonate (`text(Na)_2text(CO)_3`) solution. When the `text(two)` solutions were mixed, a reaction occurred that formed `text(two)` new substances, a magnesium carbonate (`text(MgCO)_3`) solid and a sodium sulfate (`text(Na)_2text(SO)_4`) solution. The equation for the reaction is shown:
:ibox:`text(MgSO)_4+text(Na)_2text(CO)_3->text(MgCO)_3+text(Na)_2text(SO)_4`
How did mass change during the reaction?

A.Choice: Mass increased because some new atoms in the products are created during the chemical reaction.

B.Choice: Mass stayed the same because the total number of atoms in the reactants and the total number of atoms in the products are the same.

C.Choice: Mass decreased because some of the atoms of the reactants are destroyed during the chemical reaction.

D.Choice: Mass increased because the total number of atoms in the liquid reactants is less than the total number of atoms in the solid and liquid products.
